data.name: Emmerholt: Prologue
data.detailed_description:
This is the prologue of Emmerholt - an upcoming open world, magic wielding, story driven, adventure game for the HTC Vive, and Oculus Touch. Currently in development by Oneiric Entertainment!

In this prologue follow along the journey of Eli, a young man whom has lived a peaceful life with his friends on a small island off the coast of the mainland. On this night however, something strange takes place on the island that would change Eli's fate forever.

This free demo is meant to act as a prologue for the upcoming game Emmerholt. We are releasing this to get feedback and to see what the community thinks about our locomotion mechanics, gameplay, and story.

Full Version Coming in late 2017:
Emmerholt will be a free-roaming adventure game with numerous side quests and missions. Bustling cities and towns exist there with a diverse set of factions to encounter. The game will be story focused with emotional well written quests and a talented pool of voice actors. Unlock powerful magic which can be used at will during and outside of combat. Use the intuitive horseback riding mechanic to travel across the world.

pc_requirements.minimum:
Mínimos:
  • Sistema Operativo *: Windows 7 SP1 (64 bit) or higher
  • Processador: Intel Core i5 4590 equivalent or higher
  • Memória: 8 GB de RAM
  • Placa gráfica: Nvidia GeForce GTX 970 equivalent or higher
  • DirectX: Versão 11
  • Espaço no disco: Requer 3 GB de espaço livre
  • Compatibilidade com R.V.: SteamVR or Oculus PC. Standing or Room Scale

reviews.review:
Pros:
-Simple graphics, good for people with a lower end graphics cards and i like the style of it.
-Horse riding, this was the first time i have experienced this way of traveling in a VR game and i really enjoyed it, luckily i don't get motion sick but there should definitly be a skip, fast travel or something like it button for people who do get motion sick very quickly.
-world design, very fantasy like, fits well with the graphics, nice colors.

Neutral:
-picking up objects with the power was cool but since you cannot move the object closer or further i found it quite annoying after some time.
-Voice acting was fine, but the characters need some kind of mouth movement when talking, even if it's very basic and automated.
-No menu for graphics settings, volume, etc, not a con of the game but i felt like the graphics could use some upscalling to get rid of the blurry effect.

Cons:
-The fighting, only being able to throw rocks and use a shield which i didn't even know if it did damage or not was annoying.
-The conversation circle, you can't walk past a certain distance if you are talking with the main NPC's, i do not think this should be a part of the full game, i think it's better to replace it with the NPC's just pausing until you come back into hearing range.
-Horse riding controls, while adjusting the Vive headset the horse came to a complete stop, it would be better if it slowed down a bit or if you would need to make a faster movement to make it go slower / stop.

Even though it was only 20 - 30 minutes long i really enjoyed it, when the full game releases i would be very interested in buying it, even if it costs more then the average VR game.
I would say this is a great example of what future open world adventure VR games should look like.
